+name: Browser fixture audit
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [labeled]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      source:
+        description: Audit the current source or its main baseline
+        type: choice
+        options: [candidate, baseline]
+        default: candidate
+      baseline:
+        description: Immutable baseline commit (required for a manual baseline audit)
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  audit:
+    if: >-
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
+       (github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-baseline' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-audit'))
+    name: Fixture audit (${{ matrix.project }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        project: [production, development, sync-production]
+    env:
+      AUDIT_SOURCE: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-baseline' && 'baseline' || inputs.source || 'candidate' }}
+      AUDIT_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+      AUDIT_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || inputs.baseline }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ env.AUDIT_HEAD }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Retain the candidate's audit driver and select immutable source
+        run: |
+          cp scripts/ci/fixture-audit.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit.ts"
+          cp scripts/ci/fixture-audit-reporter.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit-reporter.ts"
+          [[ "$AUDIT_HEAD" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
+          if [ "$AUDIT_SOURCE" = baseline ]; then
+            [[ "$AUDIT_BASE" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
+            git checkout --detach "$AUDIT_BASE"
+          fi
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
+        with:
+          node-version-file: .nvmrc
+          package-manager-cache: false
+      - name: Install pinned dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+      - name: Install pinned Chromium
+        run: |
+          node scripts/ci/prefer-ubuntu-archive.ts
+          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
+      - name: Build the selected source
+        if: matrix.project != 'development'
+        env:
+          VITE_SYNC_EVIDENCE: ${{ matrix.project == 'sync-production' && '1' || '0' }}
+          VITE_DOC_SELECTION_EVIDENCE: ${{ matrix.project == 'production' && '1' || '0' }}
+        run: npm run build
+      - name: Execute the predeclared first-attempt sample
+        env:
+          SPINEL_E2E_PROJECT: ${{ matrix.project }}
+          VITE_DOC_SELECTION_EVIDENCE: ${{ matrix.project == 'production' && '1' || '0' }}
+        run: node "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit.ts"
+      - name: Retain every attempt and process observation
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: fixture-audit-${{ env.AUDIT_SOURCE }}-${{ matrix.project }}
+          path: |
+            fixture-audit/
+            playwright-report/
+            test-results/**/fixture-evidence.json
+            test-results/**/sync-diagnostics.json
+            test-results/**/phone-doc-caret-events*.json
+            test-results/**/phone-doc-selection-evidence*.json
+            test-results/**/test-failed-*.png
+            test-results/**/error-context.md
+            test-results/**/trace.zip
+          retention-days: 14
+          if-no-files-found: error

+# SPN-120 — browser fixture first-attempt evidence
+
+## Scope and first capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment under the standing delegation.**
+The Owner requested a merge-ready PR and the repository's documented validation.
+The complete outcome remains L: the finite historical audit, verified setup,
+owned-process observations, bounded cleanup, negative controls, and a fixed
+before/after browser sample. This does not replace the browser framework or own
+runtime, native callback, storage-integrity or unrelated product repairs.
+
+Starting main is `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`. GitHub reports admin
+and push permission, and creating `codex/spn-120-fixture-reliability` succeeded.
+There was no existing SPN-120 branch or PR. The pinned runtime is Node 26.12.1;
+the lock pins Playwright 1.64.1. Actual browser identity is recorded with execution.
+
+The named scenarios use Playwright's configured servers, while other fixtures
+use `e2e/app-process.ts`. Process evidence must reach both boundaries. The
+current snapshot reader's `maxRetries: 1` is an unconditional observation retry,
+introduced in SPN-070; it does not meet the subsequent setup-only recovery rule.
+Non-authentication fixtures already seed real sessions but do not first verify
+the browser context's exact account. The two historical heading failures are
+real authentication scenarios, so their passkey ceremonies must remain intact.
+
+Operator gains useful first-attempt maintenance evidence. Owner and Collaborator
+retain exact saved/offline content and their account boundaries. Link guest
+retains scoped view-only access and immediate revocation. No product UI changes
+are planned, so new visual design approval is inapplicable; rendering and
+interaction checks remain required.
+
+## Predeclared bounded sample
+
+**Declared before execution, 2026-11-01.** Run exactly **two repetitions** of
+each row's existing scenario on the recorded main baseline and then on the
+repaired candidate: **24 first-attempt executions per revision**, fresh browser
+contexts/profiles, `--repeat-each=2 --retries=0`, one worker. Do not add repetitions
+after observing a failure. Preserve every failure and any aborted execution.
+The repair-proof sample must use no scenario retry and no setup recovery.
+Separately test exactly-one eligible setup recovery and its fatal controls.
+
+| Project | Current scenario selector | Executions per revision |
+| --- | --- | ---: |
+| production | `ordinary passkeys work without Web Locks and an old logout response cannot clear the new cookie` | 2 |
+| production | `profile signs out another browser, then verifies and removes its passkey without losing the current account` | 2 |
+| production | all four `phone Doc` light/dark × editor/guest-viewer pan/zoom cases | 8 |
+| development | the same four `phone Doc` cases | 8 |
+| sync-production | unfinished Sheet cell-draft recovery | 2 |
+| sync-production | `native Docs preserve concurrent text and undo across reconnect, render profile presence, and capture actual image UI edits` | 2 |
+
+Use the unchanged per-scenario/operation budgets, runtime pins, full content,
+caret, account, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work assertions. Primary
+latency samples keep tracing disabled. Existing first-attempt phone traces stay;
+evaluate retain-on-failure for the named other non-performance cases. Essential
+published summaries contain source/test/attempt, phase, readiness and process
+state, never session cookies, credentials or document contents. Expiring raw
+artifacts supplement the maintained disposition rather than replace it.
+
+This finite sample can establish non-reproduction under its stated conditions;
+it cannot establish absence of a rare race. A later identified repair is not
+proof of the exact historical interleaving when no original phase trace exists.
+
+## Historical inventory
+
+The [original bounded audit](ci-reliability-2026-10-28.md#failure-evidence) and
+[SPN-116's explicit split](SPN-116.md#scope-split) remain unchanged.
+
+| Original source/run/job | Recorded failure | Initial supported status |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `9b42229b130c0e4e305c34d54a28b33f376113f8`; [40598674501 / 122521092037](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/40598674501/job/122521092037) | Both named passkey cases: invitation Join to My files exceeded five-second heading assertion | Recheck current main; no historical cause established. |
+| `c2e8cac0fcdec36d992d6ebf3f377c9b579a8002`; [40469868909 / 122074199787](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/40469868909/job/122074199787) | Unfinished Sheet draft exceeded 180 seconds and context closed | SPN-055 later removed a demonstrated disappearing-Retry-button race after Escape. Original timed-out phase was not retained. |
+| `d001fb0fe106bf81a7bcd57b9b4db78de86424cb`; [40461836024 / 122048106950](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/40461836024/job/122048106950) | Native Docs saved snapshot GET reset | The later blanket retry does not establish a fix. The SPN-118 mobile redo reset is a different observation. |
+| `e1b26cc4529aff6890b1dd93c6105f0b7f358a15`; [40449582938 / 122008969704](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/40449582938/job/122008969704) | Phone editor/guest navigation or reload exceeded historical 150 seconds | SPN-072 subsequently repaired seeding/readiness; preserve current budgets and recheck. |
+| `d88f9253c3276d42397c138f960b7056d5b288f2`; [40424121801 / 121925641718](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/40424121801/job/121925641718) | Phone caret not in view | SPN-072 diagnosed color-restyling deactivation and repaired public selection synchronization; the exact old interleaving remains unproven. |
+
+Runtime abort SPN-117, native callback work SPN-113/SPN-121, and destination
+preservation SPN-118 keep their separate ownership. A newly reproduced product
+defect needs evidence and its own scope decision; this PR cannot hide it as setup.
+
+## Baseline result and supported historical dispositions
+
+All **24/24 predeclared baseline first attempts passed**, zero skipped, unexpected
+or flaky results, in [run 41340400081](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41340400081),
+attempt 1. Node 26.12.1, Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Executed source
+was main `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b` **plus the retained diagnostic-only
+snapshot `maxRetries: 1` to `0` patch**. Driver commit was `27ff4585a3efdc9b9b97064236e8791eef611f59`.
+No setup recovery was present in that baseline; the hidden observation retry was
+explicitly disabled before execution.
+
+| Project / job | First attempts | Browser-run duration |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| production / 124948958556 | 12 passed | 179.788 s |
+| development / 124948958392 | 8 passed | 212.624 s |
+| sync-production / 124948958534 | 4 passed | 53.828 s |
+
+[Maintained baseline evidence](evidence/SPN-120-baseline.json) contains each test,
+source/tree/lock/driver identity, first-attempt duration/status, the diagnostic
+patch, and independent validation against the exact manifest. All three archives
+were downloaded and their bytes matched GitHub's SHA-256. They expire November 15;
+these essential records remain in the repository. The original JSON reporter
+omits `repeatEachIndex`; its distinct timestamps/worker identities and exactly two
+records per named case are retained, with an honest report-order `sampleOrdinal`.
+The candidate's narrow reporter additionally retains real repetition indices and
+per-repetition test IDs. A reporting enhancement does not justify rerunning the
+successful baseline.
+
+The supported dispositions are **not reproduced in this predeclared sample** for
+both auth headings and the snapshot reset. Their historical cause remains unknown.
+Phone caret/navigation and unfinished-Sheet recovery also did not reproduce; the
+identified subsequent SPN-072/SPN-055 repairs above remain relevant evidence,
+without claiming that an unavailable old phase trace was reconstructed. No new
+product defect was reproduced or reassigned by this bounded audit.
+
+## Verified setup and strict observations
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment.** Existing AuthStore session seeding stays
+in non-authentication fixtures. Before feature actions, the actual browser context
+reads `/api/auth/session` and must match the intended account. Wrong/missing identity,
+401/403, expiry/revocation, malformed responses and failed assertions remain fatal.
+The true passkey scenarios retain every real enrollment/login, account-switch,
+old-cookie, cancellation and revocation check, including the original My files
+expectations. No authentication mutation receives a retry.
+
+Only the pre-feature idempotent session GET may recover once from a specifically
+recognized ECONNRESET. The same five-second setup deadline bounds both attempts
+and the intervening health read. Fresh, ready, live owned-process evidence and a
+successful `/api/health` response are required before that second preparation
+request. Both attempts and their classification are retained. Unclassified errors,
+a crashed/closing/stale server, exhausted budget or second reset remain failures.
+Independent direct-process fixtures without owned-server evidence cannot recover.
+`SPINEL_FIXTURE_NO_RECOVERY=1` makes any such reset fatal in the repair-proof sample.
+
+The prior SPN-070 snapshot-observation retry is removed: saved-content snapshot
+GETs always use `maxRetries: 0`. An observation or failed product assertion is never
+rerun as setup. This supersedes only that historical fixture-retry policy, not its
+product/security acceptance. `failOnFlakyTests`, original correctness assertions,
+scenario budgets and runtime pins remain intact. There are no arbitrary readiness
+sleeps, blanket timeout increases, skipped contracts or expected failures.
+
+Operator benefits from explicit setup identity and first causes. Owner and
+Collaborator retain exact authored/saved/offline content and account separation;
+Link guest retains denial/revocation. This scope remains independent of SPN-115.
+
+## Owned server, first-attempt phases and bounded cleanup
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment.** Reuse the existing owned-child boundary.
+`startApp` monitors complete exact readiness, cancellation, exit and bounded closure.
+Both 16 KiB stdout/stderr tails continue after readiness; public evidence contains
+only allowlisted runtime codes/headlines and safe stack locations. Unexpected exit
+and first failure survive later cleanup. TERM escalates to KILL inside the existing
+five-second total close budget; unconfirmed inherited-pipe closure fails explicitly.
+
+The normal HTTP Playwright servers use the same observer through a small wrapper.
+Its exact readiness marker is emitted only after the first atomic process record.
+A random run identity, owner/child PID, first failure and 250 ms evidence timestamps
+prevent stale output from authorizing recovery. The named scenarios observe actual
+process state, interrupt on loss, close their contexts and join the interrupted
+scenario's bounded cleanup before returning. The original error remains first and
+as the cause if cleanup also fails. Setup failures also roll back partial resources;
+fixture close is memoized. Diagnostic capture is bounded to one second, concurrent
+context closure to three seconds, with database disposal always attempted.
+
+Per-test evidence records tested source, test ID, repetition, retry, phase, setup
+attempts and process state, without credentials or document contents. Both ordinary
+CI and the dedicated audit retain it. The named non-performance cases keep
+first-attempt retain-on-failure traces; primary Doc responsiveness and callback
+samples keep plain servers and tracing disabled. Existing content, account, recovery,
+rendering and interaction checks remain mandatory.
+
+## Verification checkpoint
+
+At implementation publication, the baseline and focused controls are complete;
+candidate browser acceptance, current-head full CI and both independent final
+grades are still required. The final PR description is the authoritative completion
+record for this checkpoint: it retains final check identities, exact reviewed SHA,
+per-case candidate results, all failure dispositions and both independent rubrics.
+Draft publication is not merge readiness and this request does not authorize merging.
+
+Local validation uses the pinned runtime, shared serial lock and 2 GiB / 475-second
+process-tree watchdog. After review repairs, 58 controls (including exact manifest
+negatives and joined interrupted cleanup) passed in 6.04 s total, peak 391.8 MiB.
+Four additional real HTTP/Playwright request controls passed in 7.02 s, peak
+227.5 MiB: eligible TCP reset, disabled recovery, exhausted recovery and terminated
+server. These 62 controls used no retries or skips. Integrated full typecheck
+passed in 10.10 s, peak 1,780.5 MiB; full lint, dependency-boundary and formatting
+checks passed in 30.66 s, peak 648.3 MiB. Elapsed measurements include any shared
+serial-lock wait and do not describe browser latency.
+
+Retained non-passes: sandboxed tiny-child controls lost pipes/EOF before any useful
+assertion, independently reproduced with a standalone child; identical controls
+passed under scoped process permission. Pinned Chromium's local download returned
+invalid ZIP bytes, so browser acceptance uses hosted CI. Neither is a browser pass.
+The initial documentation checkpoint's PR gate correctly failed because landing
+bookkeeping was still pending; that draft failure is not hidden or waived.
+
+Candidate `5edd3665d32f2a27f490962e5c4a004a706425ec` also exposed a collection
+error before browser scenarios ran: [audit 41342044627](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41342044627),
+production job 124953944948, development job 124953945085 and sync-production job
+124953945143 rejected a describe-level trace override. The pinned Playwright implementation declares trace as a worker
+fixture. The repair uses [fixture overrides](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures#overriding-fixtures)
+through `test.extend`, used only by each named non-performance scenario, and checks
+collection before another candidate audit. This failure is not a historical product
+reproduction, a browser pass, or evidence that the declared sample completed.
+Independent review also moved the three named journey cleanup scopes ahead of all
+awaited context/cookie/CDP setup, registering each acquired context immediately.
+That closes source-proven partial-construction leaks without changing any ceremony
+or correctness assertion. Repaired collection passed all 79 tests in the five
+affected files (5.02 s, 482.4 MiB), and full typecheck passed (8.04 s, 1,904.1 MiB).
+Collection does not execute browser scenarios. Final browser and CI validation
+must use the repaired commit.
+
+## Retained acceptance and scope limits
+
+The original ticket remains available at the immutable starting main. Its finite
+historical inventory and explicit per-case disposition are preserved above. The
+complete outcome includes readiness, eligible setup recovery and fatal negative
+controls before recovery is enabled, deterministic verified setup for non-auth
+features, bounded safe logs/cleanup, and exactly two fresh-profile first attempts
+per named scenario with no scenario retry or setup recovery. The allowed setup
+recovery is separately exercised and never stands in for repair-proof acceptance.
+
+Missing readiness, wrong-account/denied/expired authentication, retry exhaustion,
+a terminated process and failed product assertions must still fail within their
+original budgets. No runtime pin, latency/content/immutability contract or native
+callback ownership changes. An incomplete workload is not proof of lost data.
+SPN-116's shared-folder restart repair is preserved rather than duplicated. A newly
+reproduced product defect needs its own evidence-backed owner and estimate; no
+such defect is concealed by routing or reassigned to improve this PR's grade.

-# 🔎 SPN-120 Resolve the remaining recorded browser fixture failures
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Operator](../product/personas.md#operator), I want browser checks to wait for the state they actually need and explain failures, so that I can update Spinel without uncertain reruns.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### Each remaining recorded failure has a useful first-attempt result
-
-Given the recorded readiness, navigation, connection and teardown failures,
-When they are rechecked against a recorded current main, pinned runtime and browser,
-Then confirmed fixture races are repaired using observable state,
-And missing readiness or a crashed server still fails clearly with the original cause preserved.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Effort L, full-scope review 2026-10-29: Keep the finite historical failure inventory and explicit per-case disposition. Prove readiness, eligible setup-retry classification and fatal negative controls before enabling recovery; unrelated product fixes and a generic retry framework are separate outcomes. [All-ticket assessment](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#all-ticket-effort-and-impact-review).
-
-- Preserve the original SPN-116 audit after its [explicit scope split](../implementation/SPN-116.md#scope-split), agent judgment 2026-10-28, originating from SPN-118 / PR #213. SPN-116 owns only the demonstrated shared-creation restart preparation boundary; it does not establish dispositions for these remaining historical symptoms.
-- Use the [bounded failure audit](../implementation/ci-reliability-2026-10-28.md#failure-evidence), agent judgment 2026-10-28. Its auth-heading, phone-navigation, offline-recovery-close and snapshot-reset cases occurred on different historical revisions; establish their current status before changing code.
-- Record each case as reproduced, fixed by an identified later change, or not reproduced in a predeclared bounded sample. Retry success or an unrelated green run alone does not establish a fix.
-- Repair demonstrated shared fixture/state-observation races. Preserve authentication, account switching, saved content, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work contracts. Use no arbitrary sleeps, blanket timeout increases or unconditional request retries.
-- Cleanup must be bounded, tolerate already-closed resources and retain the initial failure alongside cleanup errors. Record source SHA, test/attempt, relevant readiness and process-exit state without credentials or document contents.
-- For non-authentication scenarios, use deterministic authenticated fixtures and verify the actual identity/session before the feature flow. Keep full login/passkey, denial, expiry, account-switch and revocation behavior in their own first-attempt security coverage. [Approved refinement](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#timely-and-resilient-tests), owner 2026-10-29.
-- Permit at most one explicitly classified retry of idempotent setup/transport preparation inside its existing time budget, only while the owned server is healthy; retain both attempts/reasons. Never retry an authentication mutation, wrong identity, denied/expired session, crashed process or failed product assertion as setup noise. Negative controls must prove those conditions still fail.
-- Keep a bounded post-readiness stdout/stderr tail in the shared owned-process fixture and surface unexpected exit promptly. Capture first-attempt phase/readiness/process evidence; evaluate retain-on-failure tracing for non-performance cases without instrumenting primary latency samples.
-- Retain `failOnFlakyTests` and every correctness assertion; do not skip, mark expected-failing or accept a test/scenario retry to obtain a green gate. +import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
+import type { Browser, BrowserContext, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';
+import type { AppProcessEvidence } from './owned-process.ts';
+import { withFixtureCleanup } from './owned-process.ts';
+
+export type ServerEvidence = AppProcessEvidence & {
+  ownerPid: number;
+  runId: string;
+  updatedAt: number;
+};
+type EvidenceInfo = Pick<
+  TestInfo,
+  'testId' | 'retry' | 'repeatEachIndex' | 'project' | 'outputPath'
+>;
+const journals = new WeakMap<object, { started: number; events: object[]; dropped: number }>();
+let sourceSha: string | undefined;
+
+/** No cookies, account IDs, URLs, native snapshots or arbitrary error messages. */
+export function fixturePhase(info: EvidenceInfo, phase: string, facts: object = {}) {
+  let journal = journals.get(info);
+  if (!journal) {
+    journal = { started: performance.now(), events: [], dropped: 0 };
+    journals.set(info, journal);
+  }
+  journal.events.push({
+    elapsedMs: Math.round(performance.now() - journal.started),
+    phase,
+    ...facts,
+  });
+  if (journal.events.length > 128) {
+    journal.events.shift();
+    journal.dropped++;
+  }
+  if (!sourceSha) {
+    try {
+      sourceSha = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
+    } catch {
+      sourceSha = 'unavailable';
+    }
+  }
+  const path = info.outputPath('fixture-evidence.json');
+  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
+  writeFileSync(
+    path,
+    JSON.stringify(
+      {
+        sourceSha,
+        testId: info.testId,
+        project: info.project.name,
+        retry: info.retry,
+        repeatEachIndex: info.repeatEachIndex,
+        events: journal.events,
+        dropped: journal.dropped,
+      },
+      null,
+      2,
+    ) + '\n',
+  );
+}
+
+export function serverEvidencePath(origin: string) {
+  const port = new URL(origin).port;
+  if (!/^\d+$/.test(port)) throw new Error('Fixture server needs its explicit isolated port.');
+  return resolve('playwright-report', `server-${port}.json`);
+}
+
+export function readServerEvidence(origin: string): ServerEvidence {
+  const state = JSON.parse(readFileSync(serverEvidencePath(origin), 'utf8')) as ServerEvidence;
+  if (
+    !Number.isSafeInteger(state.ownerPid) ||
+    state.ownerPid <= 0 ||
+    !Number.isSafeInteger(state.pid) ||
+    !state.pid ||
+    state.pid <= 0 ||
+    !/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/.test(state.runId) ||
+    typeof state.ready !=

+name: Browser fixture audit
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [labeled]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      source:
+        description: Audit the current source or its main baseline
+        type: choice
+        options: [candidate, baseline]
+        default: candidate
+      baseline:
+        description: Immutable baseline commit (required for a manual baseline audit)
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  audit:
+    if: >-
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
+       (github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-baseline' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-audit'))
+    name: Fixture audit (${{ matrix.project }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        project: [production, development, sync-production]
+    env:
+      AUDIT_SOURCE: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-baseline' && 'baseline' || inputs.source || 'candidate' }}
+      AUDIT_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+      AUDIT_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || inputs.baseline }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ env.AUDIT_HEAD }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Retain the candidate's audit driver and select immutable source
+        run: |
+          cp scripts/ci/fixture-audit.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit.ts"
+          cp scripts/ci/fixture-audit-reporter.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit-reporter.ts"
+          [[ "$AUDIT_HEAD" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
+          if [ "$AUDIT_SOURCE" = baseline ]; then
+            [[ "$AUDIT_BASE" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
+            git checkout --detach "$AUDIT_BASE"
+          fi
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
+        with:
+          node-version-file: .nvmrc
+          package-manager-cache: false
+      - name: Install pinned dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+      - name: Install pinned Chromium
+        run: |
+          node scripts/ci/prefer-ubuntu-archive.ts
+          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
+      - name: Build the selected source
+        if: matrix.project != 'development'

+# SPN-120 — browser fixture first-attempt evidence
+
+## Scope and first capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment under the standing delegation.**
+The Owner requested a merge-ready PR and the repository's documented validation.
+The complete outcome remains L: the finite historical audit, verified setup,
+owned-process observations, bounded cleanup, negative controls, and a fixed
+before/after browser sample. This does not replace the browser framework or own
+runtime, native callback, storage-integrity or unrelated product repairs.
+
+Starting main is `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`. GitHub reports admin
+and push permission, and creating `codex/spn-120-fixture-reliability` succeeded.
+There was no existing SPN-120 branch or PR. The pinned runtime is Node 26.12.1;
+the lock pins Playwright 1.64.1. Actual browser identity is recorded with execution.
+
+The named scenarios use Playwright's configured servers, while other fixtures
+use `e2e/app-process.ts`. Process evidence must reach both boundaries. The
+current snapshot reader's `maxRetries: 1` is an unconditional observation retry,
+introduced in SPN-070; it does not meet the subsequent setup-only recovery rule.
+Non-authentication fixtures already seed real sessions but do not first verify
+the browser context's exact account. The two historical heading failures are
+real authentication scenarios, so their passkey ceremonies must remain intact.
+
+Operator gains useful first-attempt maintenance evidence. Owner and Collaborator
+retain exact saved/offline content and their account boundaries. Link guest
+retains scoped view-only access and immediate revocation. No product UI changes
+are planned, so new visual design approval is inapplicable; rendering and
+interaction checks remain required.
+
+## Predeclared bounded sample
+
+**Declared before execution, 2026-11-01.** Run exactly **two repetitions** of
+each row's existing scenario on the recorded main baseline and then on the
+repaired candidate: **24 first-attempt executions per revision**, fresh browser
+contexts/profiles, `--repeat-each=2 --retries=0`, one worker. Do not add repetitions
+after observing a failure. Preserve every failure and any aborted execution.
+The repair-proof sample must use no scenario retry and no setup recovery.
+Separately test exactly-one eligible setup recovery and its fatal controls.
+
+| Project | Current scenario selector | Executions per revision |
+| --- | --- | ---: |
+| production | `ordinary passkeys work without Web Locks and an old logout response cannot clear the new cookie` | 2 |
+| production | `profile signs out another browser, then verifies and removes its passkey without losing the current account` | 2 |
+| production | all four `phone Doc` light/dark × editor/guest-viewer pan/zoom cases | 8 |
+| development | the same four `phone Doc` cases | 8 |
+| sync-production | unfinished Sheet cell-draft recovery | 2 |
+| sync-production | `native Docs preserve concurrent text and undo across reconnect, render profile presence, and capture actual image UI edits` | 2 |
+
+Use the unchanged per-scenario/operation budgets, runtime pins, full content,
+caret, account, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work assertions. Primary
+latency samples keep tracing disabled. Existing first-attempt phone traces stay;
+evaluate retain-on-failure for the named other non-performance cases. Essential
+published summaries contain source/test/attempt, phase, readiness and process
+state, never session cookies, credentials or document contents. Expiring raw
+artifacts supplement the maintained disposition rather than replace it.
+
+This finite sample can establish non-reproduction under its stated conditions;
+it cannot establish absence of a rare race. A later identified repair is not
+proof of the exact historical interleaving when no original phase trace exists.
+

+## Verified setup and strict observations
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment.** Existing AuthStore session seeding stays
+in non-authentication fixtures. Before feature actions, the actual browser context
+reads `/api/auth/session` and must match the intended account. Wrong/missing identity,
+401/403, expiry/revocation, malformed responses and failed assertions remain fatal.
+The true passkey scenarios retain every real enrollment/login, account-switch,
+old-cookie, cancellation and revocation check, including the original My files
+expectations. No authentication mutation receives a retry.
+
+Only the pre-feature idempotent session GET may recover once from a specifically
+recognized ECONNRESET. The same five-second setup deadline bounds both attempts
+and the intervening health read. Fresh, ready, live owned-process evidence and a
+successful `/api/health` response are required before that second preparation
+request. Both attempts and their classification are retained. Unclassified errors,
+a crashed/closing/stale server, exhausted budget or second reset remain failures.
+Independent direct-process fixtures without owned-server evidence cannot recover.
+`SPINEL_FIXTURE_NO_RECOVERY=1` makes any such reset fatal in the repair-proof sample.
+
+The prior SPN-070 snapshot-observation retry is removed: saved-content snapshot
+GETs always use `maxRetries: 0`. An observation or failed product assertion is never
+rerun as setup. This supersedes only that historical fixture-retry policy, not its
+product/security acceptance. `failOnFlakyTests`, original correctness assertions,
+scenario budgets and runtime pins remain intact. There are no arbitrary readiness
+sleeps, blanket timeout increases, skipped contracts or expected failures.
+
+Operator benefits from explicit setup identity and first causes. Owner and
+Collaborator retain exact authored/saved/offline content and account separation;
+Link guest retains denial/revocation. This scope remains independent of SPN-115.
+
+## Owned server, first-attempt phases and bounded cleanup
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment.** Reuse the existing owned-child boundary.
+`startApp` monitors complete exact readiness, cancellation, exit and bounded closure.
+Both 16 KiB stdout/stderr tails continue after readiness; public evidence contains
+only allowlisted runtime codes/headlines and safe stack locations. Unexpected exit
+and first failure survive later cleanup. TERM escalates to KILL inside the existing
+five-second total close budget; unconfirmed inherited-pipe closure fails explicitly.
+
+The normal HTTP Playwright servers use the same observer through a small wrapper.
+Its exact readiness marker is emitted only after the first atomic process record.
+A random run identity, owner/child PID, first failure and 250 ms evidence timestamps
+prevent stale output from authorizing recovery. The named scenarios observe actual
+process state, interrupt on loss, close their contexts and join the interrupted
+scenario's bounded cleanup before returning. The original error remains first and
+as the cause if cleanup also fails. Setup failures also roll back partial resources;
+fixture close is memoized. Diagnostic capture is bounded to one second, concurrent
+context closure to three seconds, with database disposal always attempted.
+
+Per-test evidence records tested source, test ID, repetition, retry, phase, setup
+attempts and process state, without credentials or document contents. Both ordinary
+CI and the dedicated audit retain it. The named non-performance cases keep
+first-attempt retain-on-failure traces; primary Doc responsiveness and callback
+samples keep plain servers and tracing disabled. Existing content, account, recovery,
+rendering and interaction checks remain mandatory.
+
+## Verification checkpoint
+
+At implementation publication, the baseline and focused controls are complete;
+candidate browser acceptance, current-head full CI and both independent final
+grades are still required. The final PR description is the authoritative completion
+record for this checkpoint: it retains final check identities, exact reviewed SHA,
+per-case candidate results, all failure dispositions and both independent rubrics.
+Draft publication is not merge readiness and this request does not authorize merging.
+
+Local validation uses the pinned runtime, shared serial lock and 2 GiB / 475-second
+process-tree watchdog. After review repairs, 58 controls (including exact manifest
+negatives and joined interrupted cleanup) passed in 6.04 s total, peak 391.8 MiB.
+Four additional real HTTP/Playwright request controls passed in 7.02 s, peak
+227.5 MiB: eligible TCP reset, disabled recovery, exhausted recovery and terminated
+server. These 62 controls used no retries or skips. Integrated full typecheck
+passed in 10.10 s, peak 1,780.5 MiB; full lint, dependency-boundary and formatting
+checks passed in 30.66 s, peak 648.3 MiB. Elapsed measurements include any shared
+serial-lock wait and do not describe browser latency.
+
+Retained non-passes: sandboxed tiny-child controls lost pipes/EOF before any useful
+assertion, independently reproduced with a standalone child; identical controls
+passed under scoped process permission. Pinned Chromium's local download returned
+invalid ZIP bytes, so browser acceptance uses hosted CI. Neither is a browser pass.
+The initial documentation checkpoint's PR gate correctly failed because landing
+bookkeeping was still pending; that draft failure is not hidden or waived.
+
+Candidate `5edd3665d32f2a27f490962e5c4a004a706425ec` also exposed a collection
+error before browser scenarios ran: [audit 41342044627](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41342044627),
+production job 124953944948, development job 124953945085 and sync-production job
+124953945143 rejected a describe-level trace override. The pinned Playwright implementation declares trace as a worker
+fixture. The repair uses [fixture overrides](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures#overriding-fixtures)
+through `test.extend`, used only by each named non-performance scenario, and checks
+collection before another candidate audit. This failure is not a historical product
+reproduction, a browser pass, or evidence that the declared sample completed.
+Independent review also moved the three named journey cleanup scopes ahead of all
+awaited context/cookie/CDP setup, registering each acquired context immediately.
+That closes source-proven partial-construction leaks without changing any ceremony
+or correctness assertion. Repaired collection passed all 79 tests in the five
+affected files (5.02 s, 482.4 MiB), and full typecheck passed (8.04 s, 1,904.1 MiB).
+Collection does not execute browser scenarios. Final browser and CI validation
+must use the repaired commit.
+
+## Retained acceptance and scope limits
+
+The original ticket remains available at the immutable starting main. Its finite
+historical inventory and explicit per-case disposition are preserved above. The
+complete outcome includes readiness, eligible setup recovery and fatal negative
+controls before recovery is enabled, deterministic verified setup for non-auth
+features, bounded safe logs/cleanup, and exactly two fresh-profile first attempts
+per named scenario with no scenario retry or setup recovery. The allowed setup
+recovery is separately exercised and never stands in for repair-proof acceptance.
+
+Missing readiness, wrong-account/denied/expired authentication, retry exhaustion,
+a terminated process and failed product assertions must still fail within their
+original budgets. No runtime pin, latency/content/immutability contract or native
+callback ownership changes. An incomplete workload is not proof of lost data.
+SPN-116's shared-folder restart repair is preserved rather than duplicated. A newly
+reproduced product defect needs its own evidence-backed owner and estimate; no
+such defect is concealed by routing or reassigned to improve this PR's grade.

-# 🔎 SPN-120 Resolve the remaining recorded browser fixture failures
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Operator](../product/personas.md#operator), I want browser checks to wait for the state they actually need and explain failures, so that I can update Spinel without uncertain reruns.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### Each remaining recorded failure has a useful first-attempt result
-
-Given the recorded readiness, navigation, connection and teardown failures,
-When they are rechecked against a recorded current main, pinned runtime and browser,
-Then confirmed fixture races are repaired using observable state,
-And missing readiness or a crashed server still fails clearly with the original cause preserved.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Effort L, full-scope review 2026-10-29: Keep the finite historical failure inventory and explicit per-case disposition. Prove readiness, eligible setup-retry classification and fatal negative controls before enabling recovery; unrelated product fixes and a generic retry framework are separate outcomes. [All-ticket assessment](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#all-ticket-effort-and-impact-review).
-
-- Preserve the original SPN-116 audit after its [explicit scope split](../implementation/SPN-116.md#scope-split), agent judgment 2026-10-28, originating from SPN-118 / PR #213. SPN-116 owns only the demonstrated shared-creation restart preparation boundary; it does not establish dispositions for these remaining historical symptoms.
-- Use the [bounded failure audit](../implementation/ci-reliability-2026-10-28.md#failure-evidence), agent judgment 2026-10-28. Its auth-heading, phone-navigation, offline-recovery-close and snapshot-reset cases occurred on different historical revisions; establish their current status before changing code.
-- Record each case as reproduced, fixed by an identified later change, or not reproduced in a predeclared bounded sample. Retry success or an unrelated green run alone does not establish a fix.
-- Repair demonstrated shared fixture/state-observation races. Preserve authentication, account switching, saved content, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work contracts. Use no arbitrary sleeps, blanket timeout increases or unconditional request retries.
-- Cleanup must be bounded, tolerate already-closed resources and retain the initial failure alongside cleanup errors. Record source SHA, test/attempt, relevant readiness and process-exit state without credentials or document contents.
-- For non-authentication scenarios, use deterministic authenticated fixtures and verify the actual identity/session before the feature flow. Keep full login/passkey, denial, expiry, account-switch and revocation behavior in their own first-attempt security coverage. [Approved refinement](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#timely-and-resilient-tests), owner 2026-10-29.
-- Permit at most one explicitly classified retry of idempotent setup/transport preparation inside its existing time budget, only while the owned server is healthy; retain both attempts/reasons. Never retry an authentication mutation, wrong identity, denied/expired session, crashed process or failed product assertion as setup noise. Negative controls must prove those conditions still fail.
-- Keep a bounded post-readiness stdout/stderr tail in the shared owned-process fixture and surface unexpected exit promptly. Capture first-attempt phase/readiness/process evidence; evaluate retain-on-failure tracing for non-performance cases without instrumenting primary latency samples.
-- Retain `failOnFlakyTests` and every correctness assertion; do not skip, mark expected-failing or accept a test/scenario retry to obtain a green gate. The narrowly classified setup recovery above remains inside one scenario attempt and cannot rerun a failed assertion. Keep runtime crashes, storage-integrity investigations and native callback work under their own ownership; diagnose a product defect before assigning its repair.
-- This is independent of SPN-115 routing. Operator gets reliable maintenance evidence; Owner, Collaborator and Link guest retain the existing content and access gates.
-- Keep L scope to the named historical cases and shared setup/process boundary. A newly reproduced product defect receives its own evidence-backed owner and estimate; do not expand this into a replacement test framework or an open-ended every-test rewrite.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Changing runtime pins, weakening latency/content/immutability contracts, repairing native callback ownership, or treating an uncompleted typing workload as proven data loss.
-- Duplicating SPN-116's confirmed shared-creation restart readiness repair.
-
-## Verify
-
-- Choose and record a small fixed repetition count before execution, using fresh profiles and first attempts for each affected scenario. Require that repair-proof sample to pass without test/scenario retries or setup recovery; retain every attempt and report its limits. Separately exercise the allowed setup-recovery path and record both preparation attempts; recovered setup alone does not prove the historical race fixed.
-- Withheld readiness, wrong-account/denied authentication, retry exhaustion and a terminated server must still fail clearly within the original budget. Verify bounded logs and cleanup with the first cause preserved. Run required final-SHA checks and record each original failure's supported disposition.

+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
+import type { Browser, BrowserContext, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';
+import type { AppProcessEvidence } from './owned-process.ts';
+import { withFixtureCleanup } from './owned-process.ts';
+
+export type ServerEvidence = AppProcessEvidence & {
+  ownerPid: number;
+  runId: string;
+  updatedAt: number;
+};
+type EvidenceInfo = Pick<
+  TestInfo,
+  'testId' | 'retry' | 'repeatEachIndex' | 'project' | 'outputPath'
+>;
+const journals = new WeakMap<object, { started: number; events: object[]; dropped: number }>();
+let sourceSha: string | undefined;
+
+/** No cookies, account IDs, URLs, native snapshots or arbitrary error messages. */
+export function fixturePhase(info: EvidenceInfo, phase: string, facts: object = {}) {
+  let journal = journals.get(info);
+  if (!journal) {
+    journal = { started: performance.now(), events: [], dropped: 0 };
+    journals.set(info, journal);
+  }
+  journal.events.push({
+    elapsedMs: Math.round(performance.now() - journal.started),
+    phase,
+    ...facts,
+  });
+  if (journal.events.length > 128) {
+    journal.events.shift();
+    journal.dropped++;
+  }
+  if (!sourceSha) {
+    try {
+      sourceSha = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
+    } catch {
+      sourceSha = 'unavailable';
+    }
+  }
+  const path = info.outputPath('fixture-evidence.json');
+  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
+  writeFileSync(
+    path,
+    JSON.stringify(
+      {
+        sourceSha,
+        testId: info.testId,
+        project: info.project.name,
+        retry: info.retry,
+        repeatEachIndex: info.repeatEachIndex,
+        events: journal.events,
+        dropped: journal.dropped,
+      },
+      null,
+      2,
+    ) + '\n',
+  );
+}
+
+export function serverEvidencePath(origin: string) {
+  const port = new URL(origin).port;
+  if (!/^\d+$/.test(port)) throw new Error('Fixture server needs its explicit isolated port.');
+  return resolve('playwright-report', `server-${port}.json`);
+}
+
+export function readServerEvidence(origin: string): ServerEvidence {
+  const state = JSON.parse(readFileSync(serverEvidencePath(origin), 'utf8')) as ServerEvidence;
+  if (
+    !Number.isSafeInteger(state.ownerPid) ||
+    state.ownerPid <= 0 ||
+    !Number.isSafeInteger(state.pid) ||
+    !state.pid ||
+    state.pid <= 0 ||
+    !/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/.test(state.runId) ||
+    typeof state.ready !=

+name: Browser fixture audit
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [labeled]
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      source:
+        description: Audit the current source or its main baseline
+        type: choice
+        options: [candidate, baseline]
+        default: candidate
+      baseline:
+        description: Immutable baseline commit (required for a manual baseline audit)
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  audit:
+    if: >-
+      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
+      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
+       (github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-baseline' ||
+        github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-audit'))
+    name: Fixture audit (${{ matrix.project }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 20
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        project: [production, development, sync-production]
+    env:
+      AUDIT_SOURCE: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'ci-fixture-baseline' && 'baseline' || inputs.source || 'candidate' }}
+      AUDIT_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+      AUDIT_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || inputs.baseline }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ env.AUDIT_HEAD }}
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Retain the candidate's audit driver and select immutable source
+        run: |
+          cp scripts/ci/fixture-audit.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit.ts"
+          cp scripts/ci/fixture-audit-reporter.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit-reporter.ts"
+          [[ "$AUDIT_HEAD" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
+          if [ "$AUDIT_SOURCE" = baseline ]; then
+            [[ "$AUDIT_BASE" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{40}$ ]]
+            git checkout --detach "$AUDIT_BASE"
+          fi
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7
+        with:
+          node-version-file: .nvmrc
+          package-manager-cache: false
+      - name: Install pinned dependencies
+        run: npm ci
+      - name: Install pinned Chromium
+        run: |
+          node scripts/ci/prefer-ubuntu-archive.ts
+          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
+      - name: Build the selected source
+        if: matrix.project != 'development'
+        env:
+          VITE_SYNC_EVIDENCE: ${{ matrix.project == 'sync-production' && '1' || '0' }}
+          VITE_DOC_SELECTION_EVIDENCE: ${{ matrix.project == 'production' && '1' || '0' }}
+        run: npm run build
+      - name: Execute the predeclared first-attempt sample
+        env:
+          SPINEL_E2E_PROJECT: ${{ matrix.project }}
+          VITE_DOC_SELECTION_EVIDENCE: ${{ matrix.project == 'production' && '1' || '0' }}
+        run: node "$RUNNER_TEMP/fixture-audit.ts"
+      - name: Retain every attempt and process observation
+        if: always()

+# SPN-120 — browser fixture first-attempt evidence
+
+## Scope and first capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment under the standing delegation.**
+The Owner requested a merge-ready PR and the repository's documented validation.
+The complete outcome remains L: the finite historical audit, verified setup,
+owned-process observations, bounded cleanup, negative controls, and a fixed
+before/after browser sample. This does not replace the browser framework or own
+runtime, native callback, storage-integrity or unrelated product repairs.
+
+Starting main is `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`. GitHub reports admin
+and push permission, and creating `codex/spn-120-fixture-reliability` succeeded.
+There was no existing SPN-120 branch or PR. The pinned runtime is Node 26.12.1;
+the lock pins Playwright 1.64.1. Actual browser identity is recorded with execution.
+
+The named scenarios use Playwright's configured servers, while other fixtures
+use `e2e/app-process.ts`. Process evidence must reach both boundaries. The
+current snapshot reader's `maxRetries: 1` is an unconditional observation retry,
+introduced in SPN-070; it does not meet the subsequent setup-only recovery rule.
+Non-authentication fixtures already seed real sessions but do not first verify
+the browser context's exact account. The two historical heading failures are
+real authentication scenarios, so their passkey ceremonies must remain intact.
+
+Operator gains useful first-attempt maintenance evidence. Owner and Collaborator
+retain exact saved/offline content and their account boundaries. Link guest
+retains scoped view-only access and immediate revocation. No product UI changes
+are planned, so new visual design approval is inapplicable; rendering and
+interaction checks remain required.
+
+## Predeclared bounded sample
+
+**Declared before execution, 2026-11-01.** Run exactly **two repetitions** of
+each row's existing scenario on the recorded main baseline and then on the
+repaired candidate: **24 first-attempt executions per revision**, fresh browser
+contexts/profiles, `--repeat-each=2 --retries=0`, one worker. Do not add repetitions
+after observing a failure. Preserve every failure and any aborted execution.
+The repair-proof sample must use no scenario retry and no setup recovery.
+Separately test exactly-one eligible setup recovery and its fatal controls.
+
+| Project | Current scenario selector | Executions per revision |
+| --- | --- | ---: |
+| production | `ordinary passkeys work without Web Locks and an old logout response cannot clear the new cookie` | 2 |
+| production | `profile signs out another browser, then verifies and removes its passkey without losing the current account` | 2 |
+| production | all four `phone Doc` light/dark × editor/guest-viewer pan/zoom cases | 8 |
+| development | the same four `phone Doc` cases | 8 |
+| sync-production | unfinished Sheet cell-draft recovery | 2 |
+| sync-production | `native Docs preserve concurrent text and undo across reconnect, render profile presence, and capture actual image UI edits` | 2 |
+
+Use the unchanged per-scenario/operation budgets, runtime pins, full content,
+caret, account, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work assertions. Primary
+latency samples keep tracing disabled. Existing first-attempt phone traces stay;
+evaluate retain-on-failure for the named other non-performance cases. Essential
+published summaries contain source/test/attempt, phase, readiness and process
+state, never session cookies, credentials or document contents. Expiring raw
+artifacts supplement the maintained disposition rather than replace it.
+
+This finite sample can establish non-reproduction under its stated conditions;
+it cannot establish absence of a rare race. A later identified repair is not
+proof of the exact historical interleaving when no original phase trace exists.

+## Verified setup and strict observations
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment.** Existing AuthStore session seeding stays
+in non-authentication fixtures. Before feature actions, the actual browser context
+reads `/api/auth/session` and must match the intended account. Wrong/missing identity,
+401/403, expiry/revocation, malformed responses and failed assertions remain fatal.
+The true passkey scenarios retain every real enrollment/login, account-switch,
+old-cookie, cancellation and revocation check, including the original My files
+expectations. No authentication mutation receives a retry.
+
+Only the pre-feature idempotent session GET may recover once from a specifically
+recognized ECONNRESET. The same five-second setup deadline bounds both attempts
+and the intervening health read. Fresh, ready, live owned-process evidence and a
+successful `/api/health` response are required before that second preparation
+request. Both attempts and their classification are retained. Unclassified errors,
+a crashed/closing/stale server, exhausted budget or second reset remain failures.
+Independent direct-process fixtures without owned-server evidence cannot recover.
+`SPINEL_FIXTURE_NO_RECOVERY=1` makes any such reset fatal in the repair-proof sample.
+
+The prior SPN-070 snapshot-observation retry is removed: saved-content snapshot
+GETs always use `maxRetries: 0`. An observation or failed product assertion is never
+rerun as setup. This supersedes only that historical fixture-retry policy, not its
+product/security acceptance. `failOnFlakyTests`, original correctness assertions,
+scenario budgets and runtime pins remain intact. There are no arbitrary readiness
+sleeps, blanket timeout increases, skipped contracts or expected failures.
+
+Operator benefits from explicit setup identity and first causes. Owner and
+Collaborator retain exact authored/saved/offline content and account separation;
+Link guest retains denial/revocation. This scope remains independent of SPN-115.
+
+## Owned server, first-attempt phases and bounded cleanup
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment.** Reuse the existing owned-child boundary.
+`startApp` monitors complete exact readiness, cancellation, exit and bounded closure.
+Both 16 KiB stdout/stderr tails continue after readiness; public evidence contains
+only allowlisted runtime codes/headlines and safe stack locations. Unexpected exit
+and first failure survive later cleanup. TERM escalates to KILL inside the existing
+five-second total close budget; unconfirmed inherited-pipe closure fails explicitly.
+
+The normal HTTP Playwright servers use the same observer through a small wrapper.
+Its exact readiness marker is emitted only after the first atomic process record.
+A random run identity, owner/child PID, first failure and 250 ms evidence timestamps
+prevent stale output from authorizing recovery. The named scenarios observe actual
+process state, interrupt on loss, close their contexts and join the interrupted
+scenario's bounded cleanup before returning. The original error remains first and
+as the cause if cleanup also fails. Setup failures also roll back partial resources;
+fixture close is memoized. Diagnostic capture is bounded to one second, concurrent
+context closure to three seconds, with database disposal always attempted.
+
+Per-test evidence records tested source, test ID, repetition, retry, phase, setup
+attempts and process state, without credentials or document contents. Both ordinary
+CI and the dedicated audit retain it. The named non-performance cases keep
+first-attempt retain-on-failure traces; primary Doc responsiveness and callback
+samples keep plain servers and tracing disabled. Existing content, account, recovery,
+rendering and interaction checks remain mandatory.
+
+## Verification checkpoint
+
+At implementation publication, the baseline and focused controls are complete;
+candidate browser acceptance, current-head full CI and both independent final
+grades are still required. The final PR description is the authoritative completion
+record for this checkpoint: it retains final check identities, exact reviewed SHA,
+per-case candidate results, all failure dispositions and both independent rubrics.
+Draft publication is not merge readiness and this request does not authorize merging.
+
+Local validation uses the pinned runtime, shared serial lock and 2 GiB / 475-second
+process-tree watchdog. After review repairs, 58 controls (including exact manifest
+negatives and joined interrupted cleanup) passed in 6.04 s total, peak 391.8 MiB.
+Four additional real HTTP/Playwright request controls passed in 7.02 s, peak
+227.5 MiB: eligible TCP reset, disabled recovery, exhausted recovery and terminated
+server. These 62 controls used no retries or skips. Integrated full typecheck
+passed in 10.10 s, peak 1,780.5 MiB; full lint, dependency-boundary and formatting
+checks passed in 30.66 s, peak 648.3 MiB. Elapsed measurements include any shared
+serial-lock wait and do not describe browser latency.
+
+Retained non-passes: sandboxed tiny-child controls lost pipes/EOF before any useful
+assertion, independently reproduced with a standalone child; identical controls
+passed under scoped process permission. Pinned Chromium's local download returned
+invalid ZIP bytes, so browser acceptance uses hosted CI. Neither is a browser pass.
+The initial documentation checkpoint's PR gate correctly failed because landing
+bookkeeping was still pending; that draft failure is not hidden or waived.
+
+Candidate `5edd3665d32f2a27f490962e5c4a004a706425ec` also exposed a collection
+error before browser scenarios ran: [audit 41342044627](https://github.com/mxbaylee/spinel/actions/runs/41342044627),
+production job 124953944948, development job 124953945085 and sync-production job
+124953945143 rejected a describe-level trace override. The pinned Playwright implementation declares trace as a worker
+fixture. The repair uses [fixture overrides](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures#overriding-fixtures)
+through `test.extend`, used only by each named non-performance scenario, and checks
+collection before another candidate audit. This failure is not a historical product
+reproduction, a browser pass, or evidence that the declared sample completed.
+Independent review also moved the three named journey cleanup scopes ahead of all
+awaited context/cookie/CDP setup, registering each acquired context immediately.
+That closes source-proven partial-construction leaks without changing any ceremony
+or correctness assertion. Repaired collection passed all 79 tests in the five
+affected files (5.02 s, 482.4 MiB), and full typecheck passed (8.04 s, 1,904.1 MiB).
+Collection does not execute browser scenarios. Final browser and CI validation
+must use the repaired commit.
+
+## Retained acceptance and scope limits
+
+The original ticket remains available at the immutable starting main. Its finite
+historical inventory and explicit per-case disposition are preserved above. The
+complete outcome includes readiness, eligible setup recovery and fatal negative
+controls before recovery is enabled, deterministic verified setup for non-auth
+features, bounded safe logs/cleanup, and exactly two fresh-profile first attempts
+per named scenario with no scenario retry or setup recovery. The allowed setup
+recovery is separately exercised and never stands in for repair-proof acceptance.
+
+Missing readiness, wrong-account/denied/expired authentication, retry exhaustion,
+a terminated process and failed product assertions must still fail within their
+original budgets. No runtime pin, latency/content/immutability contract or native
+callback ownership changes. An incomplete workload is not proof of lost data.
+SPN-116's shared-folder restart repair is preserved rather than duplicated. A newly
+reproduced product defect needs its own evidence-backed owner and estimate; no
+such defect is concealed by routing or reassigned to improve this PR's grade.

-# 🔎 SPN-120 Resolve the remaining recorded browser fixture failures
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Operator](../product/personas.md#operator), I want browser checks to wait for the state they actually need and explain failures, so that I can update Spinel without uncertain reruns.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### Each remaining recorded failure has a useful first-attempt result
-
-Given the recorded readiness, navigation, connection and teardown failures,
-When they are rechecked against a recorded current main, pinned runtime and browser,
-Then confirmed fixture races are repaired using observable state,
-And missing readiness or a crashed server still fails clearly with the original cause preserved.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Effort L, full-scope review 2026-10-29: Keep the finite historical failure inventory and explicit per-case disposition. Prove readiness, eligible setup-retry classification and fatal negative controls before enabling recovery; unrelated product fixes and a generic retry framework are separate outcomes. [All-ticket assessment](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#all-ticket-effort-and-impact-review).
-
-- Preserve the original SPN-116 audit after its [explicit scope split](../implementation/SPN-116.md#scope-split), agent judgment 2026-10-28, originating from SPN-118 / PR #213. SPN-116 owns only the demonstrated shared-creation restart preparation boundary; it does not establish dispositions for these remaining historical symptoms.
-- Use the [bounded failure audit](../implementation/ci-reliability-2026-10-28.md#failure-evidence), agent judgment 2026-10-28. Its auth-heading, phone-navigation, offline-recovery-close and snapshot-reset cases occurred on different historical revisions; establish their current status before changing code.
-- Record each case as reproduced, fixed by an identified later change, or not reproduced in a predeclared bounded sample. Retry success or an unrelated green run alone does not establish a fix.
-- Repair demonstrated shared fixture/state-observation races. Preserve authentication, account switching, saved content, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work contracts. Use no arbitrary sleeps, blanket timeout increases or unconditional request retries.
-- Cleanup must be bounded, tolerate already-closed resources and retain the initial failure alongside cleanup errors. Record source SHA, test/attempt, relevant readiness and process-exit state without credentials or document contents.
-- For non-authentication scenarios, use deterministic authenticated fixtures and verify the actual identity/session before the feature flow. Keep full login/passkey, denial, expiry, account-switch and revocation behavior in their own first-attempt security coverage. [Approved refinement](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#timely-and-resilient-tests), owner 2026-10-29.
-- Permit at most one explicitly classified retry of idempotent setup/transport preparation inside its existing time budget, only while the owned server is healthy; retain both attempts/reasons. Never retry an authentication mutation, wrong identity, denied/expired session, crashed process or failed product assertion as setup noise. Negative controls must prove those conditions still fail.
-- Keep a bounded post-readiness stdout/stderr tail in the shared owned-process fixture and surface unexpected exit promptly. Capture first-attempt phase/readiness/process evidence; evaluate retain-on-failure tracing for non-performance cases without instrumenting primary latency samples.
-- Retain `failOnFlakyTests` and every correctness assertion; do not skip, mark expected-failing or accept a test/scenario retry to obtain a green gate. The narrowly classified setup recovery above remains inside one scenario attempt and cannot rerun a failed assertion. Keep runtime crashes, storage-integrity investigations and native callback work under their own ownership; diagnose a product defect before assigning its repair.
-- This is independent of SPN-115 routing. Operator gets reliable maintenance evidence; Owner, Collaborator and Link guest retain the existing content and access gates.
-- Keep L scope to the named historical cases and shared setup/process boundary. A newly reproduced product defect receives its own evidence-backed owner and estimate; do not expand this into a replacement test framework or an open-ended every-test rewrite.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Changing runtime pins, weakening latency/content/immutability contracts, repairing native callback ownership, or treating an uncompleted typing workload as proven data loss.
-- Duplicating SPN-116's confirmed shared-creation restart readiness repair.
-
-## Verify
-
-- Choose and record a small fixed repetition count before execution, using fresh profiles and first attempts for each affected scenario. Require that repair-proof sample to pass without test/scenario retries or setup recovery; retain every attempt and report its limits. Separately exercise the allowed setup-recovery path and record both preparation attempts; recovered setup alone does not prove the historical race fixed.
-- Withheld readiness, wrong-account/denied authentication, retry exhaustion and a terminated server must still fail clearly within the original budget. Verify bounded logs and cleanup with the first cause preserved. Run required final-SHA checks and record each original failure's supported disposition.

+import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
+import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
+import type { Browser, BrowserContext, TestInfo } from '@playwright/test';
+import type { AppProcessEvidence } from './owned-process.ts';
+import { withFixtureCleanup } from './owned-process.ts';
+
+export type ServerEvidence = AppProcessEvidence & {
+  ownerPid: number;
+  runId: string;
+  updatedAt: number;
+};
+type EvidenceInfo = Pick<
+  TestInfo,
+  'testId' | 'retry' | 'repeatEachIndex' | 'project' | 'outputPath'
+>;
+const journals = new WeakMap<object, { started: number; events: object[]; dropped: number }>();
+let sourceSha: string | undefined;
+
+/** No cookies, account IDs, URLs, native snapshots or arbitrary error messages. */
+export function fixturePhase(info: EvidenceInfo, phase: string, facts: object = {}) {
+  let journal = journals.get(info);
+  if (!journal) {
+    journal = { started: performance.now(), events: [], dropped: 0 };
+    journals.set(info, journal);
+  }
+  journal.events.push({
+    elapsedMs: Math.round(performance.now() - journal.started),
+    phase,
+    ...facts,
+  });
+  if (journal.events.length > 128) {
+    journal.events.shift();
+    journal.dropped++;
+  }
+  if (!sourceSha) {
+    try {
+      sourceSha = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
+    } catch {
+      sourceSha = 'unavailable';
+    }
+  }
+  const path = info.outputPath('fixture-evidence.json');
+  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
+  writeFileSync(
+    path,
+    JSON.stringify(
+      {
+        sourceSha,
+        testId: info.testId,
+        project: info.project.name,
+        retry: info.retry,
+        repeatEachIndex: info.repeatEachIndex,
+        events: journal.events,
+        dropped: journal.dropped,
+      },
+      null,
+      2,
+    ) + '\n',
+  );
+}
+
+export function serverEvidencePath(origin: string) {
+  const port = new URL(origin).port;
+  if (!/^\d+$/.test(port)) throw new Error('Fixture server needs its explicit isolated port.');
+  return resolve('playwright-report', `server-${port}.json`);
+}
+
+export function readServerEvidence(origin: string): ServerEvidence {
+  const state = JSON.parse(readFileSync(serverEvidencePath(origin), 'utf8')) as ServerEvidence;
+  if (
+    !Number.isSafeInteger(state.ownerPid) ||
+    state.ownerPid <= 0 ||
+    !Number.isSafeInteger(state.pid) ||
+    !state.pid ||
+    state.pid <= 0 ||
+    !/^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/.test(state.runId) ||

+# SPN-120 — browser fixture first-attempt evidence
+
+## Scope and first capability checkpoint
+
+**2026-11-01 — accepted, agent judgment under the standing delegation.**
+The Owner requested a merge-ready PR and the repository's documented validation.
+The complete outcome remains L: the finite historical audit, verified setup,
+owned-process observations, bounded cleanup, negative controls, and a fixed
+before/after browser sample. This does not replace the browser framework or own
+runtime, native callback, storage-integrity or unrelated product repairs.
+
+Starting main is `e63956c7ec214af03c825104a81f63517eb87d0b`. GitHub reports admin
+and push permission, and creating `codex/spn-120-fixture-reliability` succeeded.
+There was no existing SPN-120 branch or PR. The pinned runtime is Node 26.12.1;
+the lock pins Playwright 1.64.1. Actual browser identity is recorded with execution.
+
+The named scenarios use Playwright's configured servers, while other fixtures
+use `e2e/app-process.ts`. Process evidence must reach both boundaries. The
+current snapshot reader's `maxRetries: 1` is an unconditional observation retry,
+introduced in SPN-070; it does not meet the subsequent setup-only recovery rule.
+Non-authentication fixtures already seed real sessions but do not first verify
+the browser context's exact account. The two historical heading failures are
+real authentication scenarios, so their passkey ceremonies must remain intact.
+
+Operator gains useful first-attempt maintenance evidence. Owner and Collaborator
+retain exact saved/offline content and their account boundaries. Link guest
+retains scoped view-only access and immediate revocation. No product UI changes
+are planned, so new visual design approval is inapplicable; rendering and
+interaction checks remain required.
+
+## Predeclared bounded sample
+
+**Declared before execution, 2026-11-01.** Run exactly **two repetitions** of
+each row's existing scenario on the recorded main baseline and then on the
+repaired candidate: **24 first-attempt executions per revision**, fresh browser
+contexts/profiles, `--repeat-each=2 --retries=0`, one worker. Do not add repetitions
+after observing a failure. Preserve every failure and any aborted execution.
+The repair-proof sample must use no scenario retry and no setup recovery.
+Separately test exactly-one eligible setup recovery and its fatal controls.
+
+| Project | Current scenario selector | Executions per revision |
+| --- | --- | ---: |
+| production | `ordinary passkeys work without Web Locks and an old logout response cannot clear the new cookie` | 2 |
+| production | `profile signs out another browser, then verifies and removes its passkey without losing the current account` | 2 |
+| production | all four `phone Doc` light/dark × editor/guest-viewer pan/zoom cases | 8 |

-# 🔎 SPN-120 Resolve the remaining recorded browser fixture failures
-
-## Story
-
-As the [Operator](../product/personas.md#operator), I want browser checks to wait for the state they actually need and explain failures, so that I can update Spinel without uncertain reruns.
-
-## Scenarios
-
-### Each remaining recorded failure has a useful first-attempt result
-
-Given the recorded readiness, navigation, connection and teardown failures,
-When they are rechecked against a recorded current main, pinned runtime and browser,
-Then confirmed fixture races are repaired using observable state,
-And missing readiness or a crashed server still fails clearly with the original cause preserved.
-
-## Rules
-
-- Effort L, full-scope review 2026-10-29: Keep the finite historical failure inventory and explicit per-case disposition. Prove readiness, eligible setup-retry classification and fatal negative controls before enabling recovery; unrelated product fixes and a generic retry framework are separate outcomes. [All-ticket assessment](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#all-ticket-effort-and-impact-review).
-
-- Preserve the original SPN-116 audit after its [explicit scope split](../implementation/SPN-116.md#scope-split), agent judgment 2026-10-28, originating from SPN-118 / PR #213. SPN-116 owns only the demonstrated shared-creation restart preparation boundary; it does not establish dispositions for these remaining historical symptoms.
-- Use the [bounded failure audit](../implementation/ci-reliability-2026-10-28.md#failure-evidence), agent judgment 2026-10-28. Its auth-heading, phone-navigation, offline-recovery-close and snapshot-reset cases occurred on different historical revisions; establish their current status before changing code.
-- Record each case as reproduced, fixed by an identified later change, or not reproduced in a predeclared bounded sample. Retry success or an unrelated green run alone does not establish a fix.
-- Repair demonstrated shared fixture/state-observation races. Preserve authentication, account switching, saved content, cancellation, revocation and unsaved-work contracts. Use no arbitrary sleeps, blanket timeout increases or unconditional request retries.
-- Cleanup must be bounded, tolerate already-closed resources and retain the initial failure alongside cleanup errors. Record source SHA, test/attempt, relevant readiness and process-exit state without credentials or document contents.
-- For non-authentication scenarios, use deterministic authenticated fixtures and verify the actual identity/session before the feature flow. Keep full login/passkey, denial, expiry, account-switch and revocation behavior in their own first-attempt security coverage. [Approved refinement](../implementation/grooming-2026-10-29.md#timely-and-resilient-tests), owner 2026-10-29.
-- Permit at most one explicitly classified retry of idempotent setup/transport preparation inside its existing time budget, only while the owned server is healthy; retain both attempts/reasons. Never retry an authentication mutation, wrong identity, denied/expired session, crashed process or failed product assertion as setup noise. Negative controls must prove those conditions still fail.
-- Keep a bounded post-readiness stdout/stderr tail in the shared owned-process fixture and surface unexpected exit promptly. Capture first-attempt phase/readiness/process evidence; evaluate retain-on-failure tracing for non-performance cases without instrumenting primary latency samples.
-- Retain `failOnFlakyTests` and every correctness assertion; do not skip, mark expected-failing or accept a test/scenario retry to obtain a green gate. The narrowly classified setup recovery above remains inside one scenario attempt and cannot rerun a failed assertion. Keep runtime crashes, storage-integrity investigations and native callback work under their own ownership; diagnose a product defect before assigning its repair.
-- This is independent of SPN-115 routing. Operator gets reliable maintenance evidence; Owner, Collaborator and Link guest retain the existing content and access gates.
-- Keep L scope to the named historical cases and shared setup/process boundary. A newly reproduced product defect receives its own evidence-backed owner and estimate; do not expand this into a replacement test framework or an open-ended every-test rewrite.
-
-## Out of scope
-
-- Changing runtime pins, weakening latency/content/immutability contracts, repairing native callback ownership, or treating an uncompleted typing workload as proven data loss.
-- Duplicating SPN-116's confirmed shared-creation restart readiness repair.
-
-## Verify
-
-- Choose and record a small fixed repetition count before execution, using fresh profiles and first attempts for each affected scenario. Require that repair-proof sample to pass without test/scenario retries or setup recovery; retain every attempt and report its limits. Separately exercise the allowed setup-recovery path and record both preparation attempts; recovered setup alone does not prove the historical race fixed.
-- Withheld readiness, wrong-account/denied authentication, retry exhaustion and a terminated server must still fail clearly within the original budget. Verify bounded logs and cleanup with the first cause preserved. Run required final-SHA checks and record each original failure's supported disposition.
